name: Re-dispatch coordinator confirmed handoff → stamp agent.run.handoff on the SELF-MINTED run
description:
ADR-053 Phase 4a — the dispatched→executing trigger for a RE-DISPATCH coordinator (the dual-anchor case rule 01 cannot serve). Sibling of 01-handoff-marker.json; the two are mutually exclusive on the anchor count (01: length_eq 1; this: length_gt 1).

THE PROBLEM IT FIXES: a recovery coordinator (e.g. create-change rule 04 reject-recovery, research/06 needs_clarification recovery) is spawned via the default-inherit path, so it carries the PRIOR run's anchor (agent.run.entity_id = R1). When it then re-dispatches (decide that triggers a run_scope=new spawn), the framework MINTS a fresh run R2 (= chain.execution.<this coordinator's own loop id>) and ADDS agent.run.entity_id = R2 — graph-ingest's triple.add is a blind append (component.go AddTriple), so the coordinator now carries TWO agent.run.entity_id triples: R1 (inherited, written first) and R2 (minted, second). Rule 01's subject override $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id is FIRST-WRITTEN-WINS (execution_context.go substitution: ReplaceAll consumes the token on the first triple in slice order), so it resolves to R1 — and would stamp R2's handoff on the WRONG run, leaving R2 stuck at `dispatched` forever (rule 02's phase guard never satisfied for R2; rule 03's success stamp then can't complete it either).

THE FIX: target the SELF-MINTED run by its literal id instead of the ambiguous anchor. The minted run's id is always chain.execution.<the firing coordinator's own loop id> = chain.execution.<$entity.instance> (run_scope=new mints with RunID = firing loop id). The literal subject $entity.org.$entity.platform.agent.chain.execution.$entity.instance resolves to R2 regardless of the inherited R1, with zero dependence on triple ordering.

WHY THE LITERAL SUBJECT IS ALWAYS SAFE HERE (must-exist flip): a DUAL anchor (length_gt 1) can only arise from inherit-one + mint-one — default-inherit copies at most ONE agent.run anchor, so two anchors implies a self-mint occurred on THIS entity → chain.execution.<$entity.instance> = R2 EXISTS (the run_scope=new mint created it; idempotent-create, so it persists across later re-evaluations too). So the add_triple never targets a non-existent entity. (This is exactly the guard that lets rule 01 keep using the ambiguous subject for the single-anchor case, where chain.execution.<own-loop> may NOT exist — a between-task coordinator dispatching within an inherited run never minted its own run.)

NO COUNT=1 TIMING WINDOW: both 01 and 01b gate on rule.spawned_task != "", which is stamped LAST (after publish success — the mint stamps both anchors BEFORE the child publish). So by the time either rule's trigger holds, the count is already final (2 for a re-dispatch) → rule 01 (length_eq 1) never sees spawned_task while this coordinator is mid-mint, and only 01b fires. No double-handoff, no missed R2 handoff.

LENGTH 0 (run-less) is excluded from BOTH rules by design: a plain-chat front-door coordinator minted no run, and a lineage-only coordinator carries only lineage.run-loop-entity-id (its run is advanced by the spawning rule's firing-entity mechanics, not a self-anchor handoff). Neither needs a handoff on its own anchor.

The whole dual-anchor situation traces to the framework's additive mint (run_scope=new appends rather than replaces the firing loop's agent.run anchor); the clean root fix would be a framework change (run_scope=new REPLACE-by-predicate on the firing entity, or a deterministic newest-anchor substitution). Until that lands upstream, this rule-layer split is the local, deterministic fix. It is SUBSTRATE-shared, so it covers every pack's recovery re-dispatch (create-change, research, autoresearch, dev-via-test) at once.

metadata.role: handoff-marker for the re-dispatch (dual-anchor) case — stamps the SELF-MINTED run
metadata.sibling: 01-handoff-marker.json — mutually exclusive via agent.run.entity_id length (this: length_gt 1; 01: length_eq 1).
metadata.self_minted_run_subject: $entity.org.$entity.platform.agent.chain.execution.$entity.instance — the run_scope=new mint roots the run at the firing loop id, so chain.execution.<$entity.instance> is the run this coordinator just minted (R2). Independent of the first-written-wins ambiguity of $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id.
metadata.must_exist_safe: length_gt 1 implies inherit-one + mint-one (default-inherit copies at most one anchor), so the self-minted run always exists when this fires — the literal subject never hits a non-existent entity under the ADR-055 must-exist flip.
metadata.root_cause_upstream: Framework's run_scope=new appends (not replaces) the firing loop's agent.run.entity_id (graph-ingest triple.add). Cleaner root fix = framework REPLACE-on-mint or deterministic newest-anchor substitution; this rule-layer split is the local fix until that lands. Cross-pack (substrate-shared).
metadata.residual: The dual-anchor first-written-wins ambiguity ALSO affects the run-FAILURE rules (agent-run/05, /07 + per-pack outcome rules) when a re-dispatch coordinator fails — they would stamp the inherited run, not the self-minted one. Not exercised by the happy recovery path (no coordinator fails); the framework root fix would cover them. Tracked separately.
